clue.text: Struggle with inability to relax? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word is kept, here the front half survives

parts.note: restlessness is an inability to relax

explanation.surface: Someone who can never unwind asks whether they are only halfway restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang 'not half!' (very much), but here it keeps only the front half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle with a problem is to grapple or fight with it, a synonym of struggle.

clue.text: Put up more amenable champion for second game

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tamer means more docile and amenable

explanation.surface: A more cooperative title-holder is entered for a return match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like nominating someone, but in a down answer it turns the word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents.

clue.text: Queen's picked up laxative for driver

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: Queen Anne gives ANNE, and the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: A monarch's chauffeur has been handed a laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like collecting a prescription, but reverses ANNE'S in this down clue. Senna is a herbal laxative and also Ayrton Senna, the Brazilian Formula One driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant-based laxative and the surname of a famous racing driver, both senses packed into the definition.

clue.text: Secular Tory introduced Blunt

indicators.note: introduced means brought inside, so the Tory is put into the secular word

parts.note: laic means lay, non-clerical, secular
Con, short for Conservative, is a Tory

explanation.surface: A non-religious Conservative politician presented someone called Blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like a surname but is the adjective: plain-spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse and to the point, so blunt in its brevity.

clue.text: Despicable type stops working and leaves containers

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable, despicable man
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: A rotter quits work and walks off, leaving behind some boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is a noun: tea leaves, kept in tea caddies.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddy is a small tin or box for storing tea, which is made from dried leaves.

clue.text: Holds and locks in this fit youngster with nothing

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, fit, written here as AI
a kid is a youngster
O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A fit young person with no experience learns grappling holds.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI, the number one becoming the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art built on joint locks and throws, so holds and locks feature in it.

clue.text: Obliged to jump to support job

indicators.note: to support means to sit underneath, so in a down answer this word comes below the other

parts.note: a duty is a job or task
a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.surface: Someone is required to leap in to back up a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-bound means morally compelled, required by a sense of duty.

clue.text: One facilitates English navy seizing island on way north

indicators.note: on way north in a down answer means the letters travel upwards, so they read backwards
seizing means grabbing and holding, so the navy surrounds the island

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An English fleet captures an island while sailing north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way north' reverses the whole navy-round-island piece, which becomes NABLER after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An enabler is a person who facilitates something, making it possible.

clue.text: In which man held haggis for tossing?

definitions.text: In which man held haggis for tossing?

indicators.note: tossing means throwing about, so these letters are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish event where a competitor gripped a haggis ready to throw it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: at Highland games, events include tossing the caber, and haggis hurling is a comic sideshow.
explanation.definitionFit: Highland games are traditional Scottish sports meetings with throwing events such as tossing the caber.

clue.text: Sign boat captain (retd)

indicators.note: retd is short for retired, read here as going back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A notice on behalf of a retired skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retd' looks like the retired captain's rank tag, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of something to come.

clue.text: Striker at Old Trafford needs two contrasting wingers

definitions.meaning: Old Trafford is both Manchester United's football ground and Lancashire's cricket ground; the cricket striker is the bat
a cricket (insect) and a bat (mammal) both have wings, but are very different creatures

explanation.surface: A football club needs a goalscorer and two very different wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all football: Old Trafford is Manchester United's stadium, striker and wingers are positions. But Old Trafford is also a Test cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The bat is what strikes the ball in cricket; split as CRICKET and BAT it names two flying creatures.

clue.text: Screen first of soccer coaches

indicators.note: first of tells us to take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A football manager vets players before training them.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen liquid through a sieve is to strain or filter it.

clue.text: Enjoyed oneself, having tricked sailor — and everyone

parts.note: to have someone is slang for tricking them, so having tricked gives had
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone had fun after fooling a seaman and the rest of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Had a ball is an idiom for having a thoroughly good time.

clue.text: Doctor rubbishes any chips I munched

indicators.note: rubbishes suggests the words are trashed and their letters jumbled
munched means chewed up, so these letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A GP disapproves of the chips the speaker has been eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbishes' and 'munched' both scramble ANY CHIPS I.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician is a medical practitioner, a doctor.

clue.text: Shopkeepers rolling over beds and chests in Ayr

indicators.note: rolling over means turned around, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: cots are small beds
kist is the Scots word for a chest; Ayr is a town in Scotland

explanation.surface: Store owners flip over beds and chests in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on Scotland's west coast, flagging a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockist is a retailer who stocks and sells particular goods, a shopkeeper.

clue.text: Groom's hot stuff

definitions.meaning: to ... a horse is to groom it with a currycomb

explanation.definitionFit: Grooming a horse with a comb is currying it; a spicy dish from South Asian cooking is a curry.

clue.text: How to warm up in bed and so on, keeping quiet

definitions.text: How to warm up in bed

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the quiet letter goes inside so on

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Advice for keeping warm under the covers, and other such tips, without making a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is to lie curled against a partner's back, a cosy way to share warmth in bed.

clue.text: Mentally prepare Yankee companion opening soft drink

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: opening means cutting into, so these letters split the others apart

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An American friend opens a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' looks like a single fizzy pop, but splits into P (soft) and SUP (drink).
explanation.definitionFit: To psych oneself up is to get mentally ready for a challenge.

clue.text: Jockey awarded in time after Victoria

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shuffle about, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A rider wins a prize in good time, finishing behind a horse called Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like a rider in a race, but it is the anagram signal on AWARDED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward VII succeeded Queen Victoria in 1901, and his reign gives the Edwardian period.

clue.text: A couple occasionally query dilettante

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A pair of people now and then question a dabbler.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur dabbles in a pursuit without professional skill, as a dilettante does.

clue.text: It's mean to state how old someone is

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
age is how old someone is

explanation.surface: Asking someone's age is rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like unkind, but it is the statistical mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic average.

clue.text: Heading off, applauded what 3 did?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter, the head of the word, is removed

parts.note: clapped means applauded

explanation.surface: As a driver leaves, the crowd claps what a previous racer achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is SENNA, the answer to 3 down: Ayrton Senna, racing driver, lapped slower cars in races.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing driver laps backmarkers by overtaking them a whole circuit ahead, as Senna famously did.

clue.text: Primarily young mares king enters in African state event for them?

indicators.note: enters in means goes inside, so these letters are placed within the country

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Young mares and a monarch take part in an equestrian event in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to the young mares: a gymkhana is a riding event, so the definition leans on the wordplay's words.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is a show of horse-riding competitions, often for children and ponies.

clue.text: Rod's line snagged in spleen?

indicators.note: snagged in means caught inside, so the letter is held within the other word

parts.note: spleen means bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: A man named Rod gets his fishing line caught in an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a name, but stands for a fisherman, as in rod and line.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a person who fishes with a rod, so an angler.

clue.text: Pullover to protect classy keeper

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so the outer letters wrap round the classy one

parts.note: pull means drag, and over turns it round, giving the letters backwards
U means upper-class, so classy

explanation.surface: A sweater that keeps a smart goalkeeper warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pullover' looks like a jumper, but splits as pull (DRAG) and over, which reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard is a keeper, someone who watches over and protects.

clue.text: Perhaps rook tax money hotel collected

indicators.note: collected means gathered in, so the tax holds the hotel letter

parts.note: cess is an old word for a tax or levy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a piece is a coin, so money

explanation.surface: A con artist gathers tax and money from a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like a verb, to swindle, or a bird, but it is the chess castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is one example of the chess pieces, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Mount a rail the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a bar is a rail

explanation.surface: Someone climbs on a fence from the wrong side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb, to climb, but is a noun: a horse for riding.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, and a mount is a horse that one rides.

clue.text: Record verses about one's part in serial

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the record and verses go round the other piece

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a poem, a set of verses
one's is read as one is, and one is I, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A singer records some poems about their own role in a TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single instalment of a serialised story or broadcast.

clue.text: Newly-wed daughter left inside took offence

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the left letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married

explanation.surface: A new bride is offended to find her daughter left behind indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to bristle with resentment, like a horse jerking its head at the reins.
